claims.assertion: This is a RydeTAXI metered trip: the rider was charged $61.32 with distance billed $43.64 for 30.95 km and the actual track shows 31.0 km against a 20.6 km optimal route, so extra distance went straight into the metered fare.
The GPS record shows two off-route segments: 18:46–18:56 added 5.66 km and 19:03–19:12 added 4.78 km, totalling 10.44 km of unexplained extra distance.

The first segment (18:46–18:56) is covered by the rider's own pre-segment message: at 18:42 the driver asked 'ok if I go round via Rifle Range Road?' and the rider answered at 18:43 'Sure, your call.' before the segment began at 18:46 — a named-road authorisation that no record ties to a stop or message placing the car on Rifle Range Road.

The second segment (19:03–19:12) has no rider message before it at all: the chat record is complete with exactly two timestamped messages, both about the first reroute and both before 18:46, so nothing from the rider covers the 19:03 segment.

The driver's post-trip statement that 'the second turn-off was my GPS rerouting' is not rider consent and is not independent evidence of any traffic cause; it was written after the trip and is contradicted by the traffic record showing no incidents.

No RD-4 justification exists: no traffic incident was recorded near the route during the trip window, the only speed bands are 30–39 km/h (band 4) on BKE and PIE, and the weather was fair with 0.0 mm rain.
The unjustified 19:03–19:12 segment added 4.78 km; at this trip's per-km rate of $1.4100/km it produced $6.74 of the $14.64 excess-distance charge, which is the refund sought.
The driver already has one upheld dispute in the last 90 days (3 disputes, 1 upheld), and this trip is a second established deviation, so his account should be sent for review.

weaknesses: The first segment (18:46–18:56, F3) is not cleanly exempt either: the rider's reply 'Sure, your call.' (F10) came in answer to the driver's named-road ask about Rifle Range Road (F9), and no fact places the car on Rifle Range Road during that segment — on the rules for named-road consent this may be read as named_road_untied/G13 'undetermined' rather than as a fully exempt segment, which would open a further 5.66 km (F3) to refund or to a referral to a human.

The driver will argue the 18:42 exchange (F9–F10) was a general authorisation to avoid the jam, wrapping the 19:03 segment (F4) into the same permission; we answer that consent must precede the segment it covers (RD-5), but the judge may read the rider's 'your call' as broad.

The driver's statement (F12) attributes the second turn-off to GPS rerouting; although there is no incident evidence (F15) and band 4 traffic is at most corroborative (F13/F14), the driver may argue a jam-app reroute was reasonable.
The ride was metered, so apportioning $6.74 (F4/F5) depends on the per-km rate being $1.4100 (F5); if the tribunal uses a different meter unit rate the sum changes.
The rider's own 90-day record shows 1 dispute, 0 upheld (F17), so there is no rider-side pattern to strengthen the account of repeated misconduct.

claims.assertion: The trip is a RydeTAXI metered trip (F8), so any refund is limited to the metered mileage actually added by any unexcused segment, calculated at this trip's per-km rate of $1.41 (F5), not to the whole $61.32 fare.

Segment F3 (18:46–18:56, +5.66 km) was covered by the rider's own consent: the driver asked before leaving the optimal route, 'ok if I go round via Rifle Range Road?' (F9, 18:42), and the rider replied 'Sure, your call.' (F10, 18:43), i.e. before the segment started at 18:46, so the segment carries no refund.

The rider's 'your call' (F10) leaves the route choice to the driver for the purpose of reaching Orchard Road; a route chosen under that authority is a general route authorisation and covers the driving done to reach the named destination, not only the single road mentioned.

Nothing in the record places any stop, waiting or errand of the driver's own on F3 or F4: the only waiting billed is 0.4 min / $0.11 (F6) and the GPS record shows no stop away from the route (F3, F4), so this is not a driver_errand case.
